text:
The most powerful refutation is that Bentham’s felicific calculus falsely assumes all pleasures and pains can be measured on a single quantitative scale, when they differ irreducibly in kind and quality. This objection, advanced by Mill and others, shows the calculus is conceptually incoherent as a measure of well-being, not merely impractical. Therefore, it cannot capture what actually makes lives go well or badly.

CONFIDENCE: 92
